The Hausa name for the fermented paste made from the seeds of the African locust bean tree (Parkia biglobosa)

Dawadawa is a dried fermented seed which is locally used as a seasoning in most parts of Ghana particularly in the north and West Africa at large for making dishes. It has a characteristic strong smell. It is also used to cure a variety of medical conditions such as malaria, infections and inflammatory diseases.
